verdict.rationale: Aider's primary UI is the CLI, and it offers two programmatic paths. The `--message` flag runs one instruction non-interactively and exits (aider-docs-6, aider-docs-33), and a Python `Coder.create`/`coder.run` scripting interface executes instructions (aider-docs-7, aider-docs-34). Most options can also be set via CLI switches, config file or `AIDER_xxx` env vars (aider-docs-18), and the community confirms it is scriptable (aider-comm-15). However, nothing shows that the many in-chat commands and UI modes (e.g. /undo, /test, /architect, /ask, /model, voice, browser UI) are programmatically exposed, and probes found no OpenAPI spec (aider-probe-3). Missing for 10: documented parity mapping of in-chat commands and modes to the scripting API, a formal or stable API reference or spec, and hands-on corroboration of full parity.
